source: i would like to create a drifting game on a baseplate with courses

image_prompt.text: Walls and rails along the course edges that physically stop a car that slides too wide
Curved track elements forcing clean direction reversals, giving each course a hairpin to drift through
A standardised launch front of evenly spaced slots at the head of each course
a large flat baseplate as the ground plane the courses sit on
several separate drifting courses laid out on the same plate, built from wide sweeping curves rather than tight technical corners

layout_placement.text: The starting slots at the head of each course
Detection regions at intervals around each course for split and lap timing

notes: Classified Racing against the genre file own boundary rule. That rule says no lap and no finish means Simulation, and the prompt states neither - but a Vehicle Sim builds a shared world with hauling routes and a resource field, which is not what a drifting course is. Racing is the wrong-for-the-right-reasons answer here.
Circuit shape assumed. Drift courses are usually loops, but the prompt says only courses.
The prompt names no scoring at all, and drifting is normally scored on angle and duration rather than on finishing. Nothing in the handoff carries that.

open_questions.ask: No look was stated - should this be a night-time street scene, a daytime circuit, or bare on the baseplate as described?
Is this a race with laps and a finish, or free drifting scored on style?
How many courses, and how long is each one?

answers.ask: No look was stated - should this be a night-time street scene, a daytime circuit, or bare on the baseplate as described?
answers.answer: Keep it bare on the baseplate as described, with simple course markings and barriers.

answers.ask: Is this a race with laps and a finish, or free drifting scored on style?
answers.answer: Make it free drifting scored on style rather than a lap race.

answers.ask: How many courses, and how long is each one?
answers.answer: Build one short course that fits comfortably on the baseplate, with several turns for drifting.
